notes_list.title: Aromaticity and Hückel Criterion
notes_list.basic_overview: A cyclic, planar, continuously conjugated system with 4n+2 π electrons is aromatic and receives substantial delocalization stabilization.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Check four conditions: cyclic, planar or effectively planar, continuous p overlap, and 4n+2 π electrons. 4n π systems can be antiaromatic if planar and fully conjugated; nonplanar systems may be nonaromatic.
notes_list.examples: Benzene is 6π aromatic. Cyclopentadienyl anion is 6π aromatic. Cyclobutadiene is a classic 4π antiaromatic case when planar.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Aromaticity can be altered by protonation/deprotonation or oxidation/reduction. Heteroatom lone pairs must be classified according to whether they participate in the aromatic π system.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: 1. Count π electrons. 2. Confirm cyclic conjugation. 3. Assess geometry. 4. Apply 4n+2 or 4n criterion. 5. Compare charge state when heteroatoms are present.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: Aromatic stabilization changes thermodynamic preference and can affect reaction pathways that temporarily disrupt aromaticity.
notes_list.selectivity_and_stereochemistry: Predict aromaticity of carbocycles and heterocycles; explain substitution preference.
notes_list.common_traps: Do not count every lone pair; one lone pair may participate while another remains in-plane for some heterocycles.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
